references.text: Abraham and Abimelech make a covenant at a well, which shows the importance of water sources and wells in agreements and relationships between people in this time.
The Philistines had filled in Abraham's wells, and Isaac dug them up again – the direct context for Isaac's servants then finding a well with living water.
Jacob meets Rachel at a well, which shows the well's significance as a meeting place and for relationships between people.
The Israelites sing a song to the well in the wilderness ('Spring up, O well!'), which emphasizes the life-giving meaning of the well for God's people on their journey.
The Song of Songs uses exactly the same expression 'well of living water' (be'er mayim chayyim), showing that this expression had deep resonance in Israel's literature.
Jeremiah uses the image of a spring with living water to describe God, pointing to the spiritual meaning of 'living water'.
Jesus speaks about 'living water' to the woman at the well, linking the physical need for water to the spiritual need for eternal life.
This reference shows the direct narrative and theological connection between the finding of the well and the confirmation of God's blessing through the servants' report.
